entries.title: The meaning of belief in the Qur'an
entries.question: When I have faith in the Noble Qur'an, what then is the ruling concerning one who denies the whole of the Qur'an Majīd, either entirely or in part, or who denies a portion of the Qur'an Sharīf, either entirely or in part — whether that denial is made with the tongue or through the other limbs?
entries.answer:
Complete affirmation of the Qur'an Pāk is obligatory.

If, concerning the whole Qur'an or any part of it (a verse), a person holds the belief that it is not revealed from Allah Ta'ālā, then faith does not remain.

And if the deficiency is in action, then it will not be ruled disbelief. Faith itself is weakened and enfeebled by it, but it does not come to an end so long as the affirmation of the heart remains.

And Allah, glorified be He, knows best.
references: Sharḥ Fiqh al-Akbar, p. 205 (Kutub Khana Rahimiyya, Deoband)

entries.urduTitle: صرف کلمہ پڑھنے سے دخول جنت
entries.title: Entry into Paradise by merely reciting the kalimah
entries.question: Zayd says: although Muslims openly commit sins in the world and carry out deeds of transgression and immorality; such people pray only a few of the prayers and keep only a few of the fasts of Ramadan; they listen to sermons and admonition and yet remain heedless of the rights owed to Allah's servants; they do not discharge even the rights of inheritance, and they disregard the command of Allah and His Messenger — will such people, then, if at the time of death they recite the kalimah, or the kalimah is granted to them, go straight into Paradise at once without punishment? For Zayd says that by receiving the kalimah every sin is forgiven and a person enters Paradise immediately. Kindly explain.
entries.answer:
Zayd's saying this as a universal rule is not correct; otherwise the denial of countless texts will follow.

However, as for the person who has come to faith and after coming to faith has committed no sin — concerning him Zayd's statement is correct.

In the Qur'an Pāk it is: ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ — that is, whoever does good equal to an atom's weight will see it, and whoever does evil equal to an atom's weight will see it.

If a person has committed sins in the life of this world, and the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants stand as obligations upon him, then merely reciting the kalimah ṭayyibah at the time of dying does not bring those rights to an end. Zayd must repent of this statement of his, because this statement of his is against the Qur'an Pāk, the Ḥadīth Sharīf and the consensus of the ummah.

For the rest, this much is certainly established: that whoever recited the kalimah ṭayyibah at the final moment — that is, whose end came upon faith — for him there is the promise of Paradise, and he will certainly go to Paradise.

But that every person goes into Paradise at once and without reckoning is neither promised nor established anywhere. Rather, some people will go into Paradise without reckoning; some will go after their punishment has been carried out in full; some will go by means of intercession; some will be brought out of Hell by the permission of the Prophet ﷺ; and some Allah Ta'ālā will bring out Himself. Some will be taken out of Hell in such a state that they have been burnt and turned entirely black like charcoal. And all of these will be those whose end came upon faith.

All of this is mentioned in Bukhārī Sharīf and in many other books of Ḥadīth.
references: Mishkāt al-Maṣābīḥ, p. 140, Bāb mā yuqāl ʿind man ḥaḍarahu al-mawt
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 2/443, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, Bāb fī al-talqīn
entries.signedBy: Mahmūd, Dār al-ʿUlūm Deoband — countersigned by Niẓām al-Dīn

entries.urduTitle: کیا محض ایمان پر جنت کی بشارت ہے
entries.title: Is the glad tiding of Paradise upon mere faith?
entries.question: Concerning the verse ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ﴾ etc., a scholar stated that the position of most exegetes is that a mere believer, without righteous deeds — prayer, fasting and so on — is also deserving of this glad tiding, because a thing is not conjoined to itself. How is this in itself?
entries.answer:
If a person dies as soon as he brings faith, and the occasion for righteous deeds did not arise, then he too is included in this glad tiding under the law of Allah, on the basis of being upon the true religion.

And as for one who, after bringing faith, was given time but performed no righteous deeds, and instead remained caught up in acts of disobedience — for him entry is not forbidden as a matter of law, but he will be deserving of Paradise after punishment.

What this scholar's own argument yields is that faith and righteous deeds are separate from one another. Therefore the glad tiding will be upon the combination of the two, not upon faith alone. So to present this as proof that a mere believer deserves the glad tiding will be wrong.

And Allah knows best.
references: Mirqāt al-Mafātīḥ 1/94, Kitāb al-Īmān (Aṣaḥḥ al-Maṭābiʿ, Bombay)
entries.signedBy: Mahmūd Gangohī, assistant mufti, Madrasa Maẓāhir ʿUlūm, Saharanpur

entries.urduTitle: احکام پر عمل کرنا اعلیٰ درجہ کے مسلمانوں کا کام ہے
entries.title: Acting on the commands is the work of high-ranking Muslims
entries.question: Some Muslims say this: that not praying, not giving zakat, not keeping fasts, telling lies, watching films and taking bribes make no difference to an ordinary Muslim; that all these deeds are for first-rank Muslims to perform, and there is no need for us to perform them, because we are only ordinary Muslims; that Allah Ta'ālā is Most Forgiving and Most Merciful, and we have complete conviction that He will surely forgive us and we will surely go to Paradise. Is this correct? And what is the ruling concerning those who say such a thing?
entries.answer:
The Real, Most High, is Forgiving and Merciful, and He is also Ever-Subduing and the Avenger. He made Paradise, and He made Hell as well. He also sent down the commands, and He appointed Paradise for those who obey.

To accept one attribute of Allah Ta'ālā and not to accept another attribute is not a matter of faith. As for the things He has forbidden, abstaining from them is obligatory.

In the same way that they think the commands are for first-rank Muslims to carry out, and that we are only ordinary Muslims, they ought also to have thought this: might it not be that Paradise too is for first-rank Muslims, and that for those people who do not act there is Hell?

Therefore such a statement, such a belief and such conduct — guarding fully against them is obligatory. Otherwise, slowly, faith and Islam, all of these things come to an end.

And Allah, glorified be He, knows best.
references: Fatāwā ʿĀlamgīriyya 2/258, al-Bāb al-tāsiʿ fī aḥkām al-murtaddīn

entries.urduTitle: انکار قرآن وحدیث کے ساتھ ایمان نہیں
entries.title: There is no faith alongside denial of the Qur'an or the hadith
entries.question:
Is one who denies the Qur'an Pāk a disbeliever or not? And likewise, is one who denies the prophetic hadiths a disbeliever or not?

The questioner notes that the Qur'an says to take whatever the Messenger gives and to abstain from whatever he forbids (al-Ḥashr 7) — so if a person denies the hadiths, is that not against this verse? And the Qur'an says that he does not speak from desire, that it is only revelation revealed (al-Najm 3–4) — of what, then, would this be said? Further, how was it even known that a thing is in the Qur'an, when he has denied the hadiths? For the hadith warns against the man reclining on his couch who, when a command or prohibition of the Prophet ﷺ reaches him, says, 'I do not know; whatever we find in the Book of Allah, that we follow' — and the Prophet ﷺ said that he was given the Qur'an and its like along with it.
entries.answer:
One who finds fault with the blessed person of the Prophet ﷺ, or with any one of his lofty attributes, is a disbeliever — whether the one who does so is a Muslim, a dhimmī or a ḥarbī, and even if he did it by way of jest. He is liable to execution, and his repentance is not accepted.

There is consensus of the ummah that disrespect and contempt toward any prophet is disbelief, and that it is forbidden for the one who commits it to regard it as lawful.

As for the denial of hadith: the number of the rak'ahs of prayer is not established from the Qur'an, and in the same way the details of zakat are not set out there. There are a great many rulings whose particulars are not found in the Qur'an. Is the one who denies these, then, not a disbeliever?

And it is stated in the Kamālayn that because the Prophet's ﷺ journey to Bayt al-Maqdis is established by a definitive text, the one who denies it is a disbeliever.

So denial of what is definitively established from the Messenger ﷺ stands on the same footing as denial of the Qur'an itself, since the greater part of the detail of the sharī'ah reaches us only by way of the Sunnah.
references: Mishkāt al-Maṣābīḥ, p. 29 — ḥadīth of Rāfiʿ (narrated by Aḥmad) and of al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib
